headline: OpenAI's chief executive said the company's mission will come before shareholders if the two conflict after it goes public.
score_reason: Pool score kept: an on-record statement by the chief executive about how the company will treat investors, matched to the interview transcript; it is an intention, not an action.
importance_line: People who use OpenAI's products and investors who may buy its shares hear a stated order of priorities before any listing, but it is an interview promise, not yet tested.
summary: Vanity Fair reports, in an interview published on 5 Oct, that OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman said a nonprofit will still govern the company after it goes public and that if shareholders' interests ever conflict with the mission, "the mission is going to come first". He said he believes the two are compatible, but asked what happens if the share price falls he said "Then it falls. Maybe it falls a lot"; Yahoo Finance adds that OpenAI is widely expected to list in early 2027.
notes: Pool item is Yahoo Finance's write-up of the Vanity Fair interview; the interview itself (Part 1) was read, the quotes match, and Vanity Fair is credited and linked as the first reporter. Yahoo's own context (IPO expected in early 2027) is attributed to Yahoo. Fortune (5 Oct) separately reports that Altman said OpenAI will not list this year. Same interview as C05-09 (Musk remark).
